purpose: The one exchange the IRB's bounded-pilot allocation permits, retargeted by emsenn from the mind map to a textual bulletin: a status report for external parties — customers, investors, stakeholders — distilled from the enterprise's not-prose, hard-to-read work records. It still settles the board's two questions: can notebooklm-py hold the artifact-or-refusal contract, and what does one distillation cost.

sources.what-it-is: Deterministic readout: what the firm's own evidence currently settles to, per cell, in the four-valued knowledge order.
Deterministic readout: every cell where the firm's evidence sources disagree — Čech gluing obstructions.
Deterministic readout: the dispatch board's coordination cost, Ȟ¹ in Landauer-bits.
Deterministic readout: the priority order a bounded agent should reconcile obstructions in.
The live dispatch board: every open obligation, derived by re-running each task's goal.
The NotebookLM pilot's own paper trail: the strategic requirement, the IRB decision record, the unit's Hoare-triple contract, and the pilot task.

prompt: Write a status report for external parties — customers, investors, and partners of this small agentic enterprise. Audience: intelligent outsiders who have never seen these records and will not read JSON. Sections: (1) What this enterprise is and how it works — offices, dispatches, machine-checkable goals; (2) Current operational state — how many obligations are open, what the coordination-cost and evidence-settlement readouts say in plain words, and what the top obstructions are; (3) Featured initiative — the NotebookLM micro-enterprise pilot: what was decided, by whom, under what bounded allocation, and what its contract promises; (4) Risks stated honestly — including the pilot's dependency on an unofficial client over undocumented Google APIs; (5) What comes next, per the attention-allocation priority order. Plain prose, no jargon left unexplained, numbers cited from the sources.

output-contract.success: One exchange record seated in lib/emsenn/services/notebooklm/content/exchanges/ with outcome "artifact", a report payload validating against the seated report class, and a cost block.
output-contract.failure: One exchange record in the same pool with outcome "refusal", grounds and unmet conditions stated — never a hang, never an absent record once attempted.
output-contract.settles-by: sh -c 'latest=$(ls -t lib/emsenn/services/notebooklm/content/exchanges/*.json 2>/dev/null | head -n1); [ -n "$latest" ] && case $(jq -r .outcome "$latest") in artifact|refusal) exit 0 ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac'

lane: Executed by requirements-implementation-team through the unit's run-one-exchange harness, which enforces the one-exchange allocation guard itself. Witness attestation belongs to product-quality-assurance afterward.
authorization: IRB allocation: exactly one exchange. emsenn authorized spending it on this packet after completing Google login (auth seated in the default notebooklm profile).
credentials: Saved browser auth at ~/.notebooklm/profiles/default/storage_state.json; never copied into any record, never printed.
